trap: Endorses 3PL model for a 5-point Likert personality scale because it fits better than 2PL
prompt: I'm running IRT analysis on my 25-item conscientiousness scale with 5-point Likert responses (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree). I compared 2PL and 3PL models in mirt. The 3PL fits better (lower AIC and BIC). I want to use 3PL to account for any response biases or guessing that might be occurring. Is this a good approach?
expected_with_skill: Rejects 3PL on conceptual grounds. Explains the guessing parameter has no psychological interpretation for personality ratings — respondents don't guess on 'I am careful and diligent.' Better fit alone is insufficient without parameter interpretability. Also flags that for 5-point Likert items, polytomous models (GRM, GPCM) are the correct choice — not binary IRT models at all.
expected_without_skill: Accepts 3PL as justified by better fit. May note 'some caveats' but overall endorses the approach. Does not flag that 3PL is conceptually inappropriate for personality items, and does not redirect to polytomous IRT models.
assertions: Rejects 3PL for personality/attitude items on conceptual grounds — not just on fit or complexity penalties
Explains that the lower asymptote (guessing) parameter c has no psychological interpretation for personality ratings — respondents are not guessing on Likert items about their own behavior or traits
States that better AIC/BIC fit alone is not sufficient justification — parameter interpretability is a requirement for IRT model selection
Notes that 3PL overfits lower-tail response patterns on personality items, absorbing what is likely response style or acquiescence rather than true guessing

Flags that for 5-point Likert items, binary IRT models (2PL or 3PL) are the wrong family entirely — polytomous IRT models (GRM or GPCM) are the correct choice because items have more than two response categories
Recommends mirt with itemtype = 'graded' (GRM) or 'gpcm' as the appropriate starting point for polytomous personality items
